title: WPMS/2417/2020 of ZAHIRA BEGUM Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 2417 of 2020
Zahira Begum .....Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others .... Respondents
Present :-
Mr. Rajendra Dobhal, Senior Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. T.S. Phartiyal, Deputy Advocate General for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Rakesh Thapliyal, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Rajat Mittal, Advocate for the
Caveator.
 Reserved on : 10th August, 2021
 Delivered on : 01.09.2021
JUDGEMENT
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
(Through Hybrid Mode)
In the present Writ Petition, the petitioner, who is an
elected Pradhan of Village Panchayat Dhakrani, Block Vikas Nagar,
District Dehradun, has put a challenge to the impugned order dated 4th
December, 2020, as it has been passed by respondent No. 2, i.e. the
District Magistrate, Dehradun, whereby, as a consequence thereto, in
view of the aforesaid order, the District Magistrate, had taken over the
charge of the Office of Gram Pradhan, from the petitioner and has
handed over it to the Deputy Pradhan of Village Panchayat Dhakrani,
Block Vikas Nagar, Dehradun, apparently, shown to have been passed
in exercise of his powers under Section 138 (1) (c) of the Panchayati
Raj Act, as applicable to the State of Uttarakhand, called as
"Uttarakhand Panchayati Raj Act of 2016", (hereinafter to be referred
as "Act No. 11 of 2016"). Besides this, the petitioner has also sought
a prayer by way of a writ of mandamus directing the respondents, not
to cause or create any hindrance in the peaceful functioning of the
petitioner as Pradhan of the said village, and in discharge of his duties
attached to the Office of Pradhan.
2. The brief facts, as engages consideration in the present
Writ Petition, are that the election to the office of the Pradhan under

2
the three-tier system, the election was held on 23rd October, 2019.
The result of the election was, thus declared on 23rd October, 2019,
was as a consequence of the election of Pradhan, which was
conducted on 22nd October, 2019, where the petitioner had won the
election of the Pradhan by 128 of votes and was declared, as a
successful returned candidate and ever since then, she has proclaimed
that she has been performing her duties of Pradhan, to the utmost
satisfaction and sincerity.
3. The petitioner has come up with the case that the
respondent No. 3, Safdar Iqbal, who was the husband of one of the
candidates, who had contested the election of the Pradhan, against the
petitioner, is said to have filed a complaint before the District
Magistrate on 5th October, 2019, whereby, it was alleged by the
complainant that the petitioner's Class-VIII certificate, which was
taken, as to be the basis of the eligibility of her candidature, to contest
the election held on 2.10.2019, was later on allegedly found to be a
forged one and, hence, in the complaint, the complainant/respondent
No.3, herein, prayed for an order of restraint against the petitioner
from exercising her power of the office of the Pradhan.
4. Questioning the election of the petitioner, which was
made as a subject matter of challenge by one of the rival candidates,
Sangeeta, a Writ Petition was preferred, before this Court, being Writ
Petition (M/S) No. 3633 of 2019, Smt. Sangeeta Vs. Zahira Begum,
which was considered on merits, by the Coordinate Bench of this
Court and the same was dismissed by the judgment of 27th November,
2019. It was dismissed on the ground that the invocation of the writ
jurisdiction, for questioning the election of the petitioner as a Pradhan
of the village, on the pretext of a doubt being created by the petitioner,
therein, in relation to her Class-VIII certificate, the Court held that in
the light of the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the
case of N.P. Nonnuswami Vs. The Returning Officer, Namakkal
Constituency, Namakkai, Salem Dist. And others reported in AIR

3
1952 SC 64 and Mohinder Singh Gill Vs. Chief Election
Commissioner, New Dehi reported in (1978) 1 SCC 405, the
appropriate recourse which would be available to the petitioner,
therein, would have been, to file an Election Petition, under the
provisions of the Uttarakhand Panchayati Raj Act of 2016.
5. Extracting this ground, about questioning the eligibility
of the petitioner and after the judgement of 27th November, 2019, an
Election Petition, challenging the election of the Pradhan was
preferred, and as per the provisions contained under Chapter-III of
the Act of 2016. After receiving the notice on the said Election
Petition, preferred by Sangeeta, the petitioner of the Writ Petition, as
referred above, which was dismissed by the Coordinate Bench of this
Court on 27/11/2019, the petitioner denied the set of allegations by
filing the written statement and was diligently contesting the
proceedings of the Election Petition, which is still pending
consideration, before the Prescribed Authority and is yet to be decided
on merits.
6. The petitioner has contended, that while defending her
election to the office of Pradhan, in the Election Petition No. 1 of
2019, Smt. Sangeeta Vs. Zahir Begum and others, she has placed the
school leaving certificate in original, which was issued by the
Madarsa Islamia Arbia Rahemia, Village Dhakrani, District
Dehraudn, and the certificate thus issued by the Principle of the said
Institute, and had also given an affidavit to the said effect that the
certificate which was issued in favour of the petitioner, by the
Institution under the signature of the Principle. But, however, the said
defence taken by the petitioner supporting his educational certificate,
is still a matter which is sub judice in an Election Petition, before the
Election Tribunal.
7. On the one hand, the Election Petition is already pending
consideration; but on account of political rivalry and in order to oust

4
the petitioner from the office of the elected Pradhan, the respondent
No. 3, had simultaneously filed a complaint before the District
Magistrate, on 5th October, 2019, yet again reiterating the same set of
allegations for challenging the election of petitioner, as Pradhan,
which was a subject matter of the pending Election Petition, which
was instituted by Sangeeta before the Prescribed Authority / S.D.M.
Vikas Nagar, District Dehradun on 7th November, 2019.
8. On this complaint thus filed, for the set of allegations, the
cognizance has been taken by the District Magistrate, vide his
correspondence made vide letter No. 2106 dated 16th March, 2020,
and he has issued a show cause notice to the petitioner under Section
138 (1) (c) of the Uttarakhand Panchayati Raj Act of 2016. The
charge No. 1, in fact, happens to be the same, which was agitated
and earlier considered by the learned Single Judge, of this Court and
later on, on the matter being relegated, she has preferred an Election
Petition, which is a matter pending consideration before the competent
Prescribed Authority.
9. It is on this complaint submitted by the respondent No.3,
to which the show cause notice, was issued to the petitioner, the
petitioner had duly filed his reply, which was received, by the office
of respondent No. 2 on 19th August, 2020, and on 1st September, 2020,
wherein, in the reply thus submitted by her, she has clearly stated,
that her certificate of educational qualification, of having passed
Class-VIII examination, was validly issued by the concerned Institute
and by the authority of competent Principle and, hence, no doubt
could be created, as far as the candidature of the petitioner for
contesting the election of the Pradhan, was concerned, on that basis of
lack of qualification, or on basis of having filed a fraudulent
certificate.
10. On the complaint of 16th March, 2020, which was
preferred by the respondent No. 3, the show cause notice, which was

5
issued was to the said subject and its effect, a reply was also called
prior to the election and even after the election was conducted, apart
from the fact that the Election Petition, which is pending
consideration, where issue as to be whether the petitioner would be
entitled and would be eligible to hold the office of Pradhan, is still a
matter sub judice.
11. On the said complaint, the District Magistrate had passed
the impugned order dated 04.12.2020, which is under challenge in the
present Writ Petition, on number of grounds, as pleaded therein in the
Writ Petition.
12. Before this Court deals with the respective contentions,
which had been respectively raised by the learned counsel for the
parties, a brief legislative backdrop is required to be considered in
view of the Constitution's 73rd Amendment Act, 1992, wherein, in its
Part 9, the Panchayats have been dealt with. It distinctly deals with
the definition of Gaon Sabha, in Sub-clause (b) of Article 243 and the
Panchayat in the respective villages at different levels under its Sub-clause (d) of Article 243 and Gaon Sabha has been independently
described under Article 243-A of the Constitution of India.
13. The Article 243-O, in fact, has created a specific bar, that
no Courts, would interfere in the electoral matters, questioning the
election of the Panchayat Act, at various levels except by way of an
Election Petition. Article 243-O, is extracted hereunder :-
"243-O. Bar to interference by courts in electoral
matters. Notwithstanding anything in this Constitution, -
(a) the validity of any law relating to the delimitation of
constituencies or the allotment of seats to such constituencies
made or purporting to be made under article 243K, shall not be
called in question in any court;
(b) no election to any Panchayat shall be called in
question except by an election petition presented to such
authority and in such manner as is provided for by or under any
law made by the legislature of a State."

6
14. On a simple interpretation of Article 243-O, where the
elected Pradhan constitutes to be an integral part of the Gaon Sabha,
as contained in Part-9 of the Constitution and its composition is
contemplated by way of the elections which has to be held by the
State, under the provisions of the Representation of Peoples Act. That
in itself provides, that a person, who has been thus elected for the
purposes of the composition of the Panchyat, as its chair person, under
Article 243-C, could not have been ousted from the Elected Office, on
the basis of the complaint of respondent No. 3, on account of the bar
which has been created by Article 243-O, as already referred above,
and particularly, in the present circumstances of the case, when on the
same set of grounds, allegations and facts, the Writ Petition was
dismissed by this Court earlier, with liberty left open to the petitioner
therein to prefer an Election Petition, and its not that even, thereafter,
an Election Petition No. Election Petition No. 1 of 2019, Smt.
Sangeeta Vs. Zahir Begum and others, was preferred, which is
pending.
15. Initiation of the proceedings, by way of a private
complaint, which was motivated and catalysed by the husband of one
of the rival contestants of the election, who has not challenged the
election of the petitioner by filing an Election Petition, apparently
would fall outside the ambit and the very spirit of Article 243-O of the
Constitution of India, because it is a settled proposition of law, that an
elected person to a local body, which is being envisaged and
mandatorily provided under the Constitution, cannot be ousted to hold
an office except with the due process of law and the due process of
law, herein, would obviously be process of law, as it has been
reserved by Article 243-O of the Constitution of India.
16. The complainant/respondent No. 3 in the present case,
when he had preferred a complaint, before the District Magistrate on
5th October, 2019, the same is apparently shown to have been

7
preferred under Section 138 (1) (c) of the Uttarakhand Panchayati Raj
Act of 2016. Section 138 (1) (c) of the Act, exclusively deals with
the powers of the State Government, who could remove the elected
Pradhan from the office of the Panchayats, under the terms and
conditions or the situation, which has been distinctly contemplated
under Section 138 (1) (c) of the Act of 2016.
17. Section 138 of the Act, as a whole, is extracted
hereunder:-
"138. Separation from their posts to the officers of the
three tiers Panchayat. - (1) The State Government may
remove a member of the Panchayats on any of the following
grounds-
(a) that he has acted as a member of the Gram Panchayat,
Kshettra Panchayat and Zila Panchayat or member of any
committee by voting or taking part in the discussion of any
matter in which he has directly or indirectly, a personal interest
or in which he is professionally interested on behalf of a client,
principal or other person;
(b) that he has become physically or mentally
incapacitated for performing his duties as such member,
Pradhan, Up Pradhan, Pramukh, Up pramukh, Chairman, Vice-Chairman;
(c) that he has been guilty, whether in his present or
an earlier term of office, of misconduct in the discharge of
his duty as such member, Pradhan, Up pradhan, Pramukh,
Up pramukh, Chairman, Vice-chairman or has contravened
any of the provisions of this Act or caused loss or damage to
the fund or property of Panchayats and such misconduct,
contravention or causing of loss or damage renders due to
conduct of work as unauthorised in place by women
representative, her husband or family members or relatives,
such women shall be in eligible as member, Pradhan Up-pradhan, Pramukh, Up-pramukh, Chairman, Vice-

8
chairman, in such case they may be suspended upto the
departmental final enquiry and their work and duties may
be hand over to a committee of three elected members of the
concerning Panchayat. In addition to the disciplinary action
also may be taken against the departmental - 276 -
employees/ officer, if found guilty in the enquiry.
[(d) The Pradhan, Up-Pradhan or member of a Gram
Panchayat or any members of Joint Committee or Land
Management Committee, or a Pramukh, Up-pramukh or any
member of Kshettra Panchayat or Chairman, Vice-Chairman or
any member of Zila Panchayat may also be removed from his
office in the following conditions -
(i) If he makes himself absent without sufficient cause for
more than three consecutive meetings or sitting or refuses to
act; or,
(ii) if he has taken the benefit of reservation under sub-section (1) of Section 10-A or sub-section (1) of Section 11,
sub-section (1) of Section 55-A or Section 56 or sub-section (1)
of Section 92-A or Section 93, as the case may be, on the basis
of a false declaration subscribed by him stating that he is a
member of the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes or the
Backward Classes, as the case may be; or
(iii) If the suffers from any of the disqualifications
mentioned in clauses (a) to (u) of sub-section (1) of Section 8,
clauses (a) to (u) of sub-section (1) of Section 53 and in clauses
(a) to (u) of sub-section (1) of Section 90.
(e) No objection shall be made in any Court on the order
made by the State Government under this Section."]
(2) Notwithstanding anything in any other enactment,
where a member specified in any member, Pradhan, Up
Pradhan, Pramukh, Up Pramukh, Chairman and Vice chairman
in clause (c) of subsection (1) of section 29 is removed from
membership under this section he shall with effect from the
date of publication of notification of removal under sub-section

9
(c), cease to hold the office of member, Pradhan, Up- Pradhan,
Pramukh Up- Pramukh, Chairman and Vice- chairman
respectively and a vacancy shall be deemed to have been
created in that office.
(3) A person who has been removed from membership of
the Panchayat under clause (a) or clause (c) of sub-section (1)
shall be disqualified for being chosen a member of the
Panchayat and being elected a member, Pradhan, Up Pradhan,
Pramukh, Up Pramukh, Chairman, Vice- chairman of a
Panchayats for a period of five years from the date of his
removal :
Provided that the State Government may, at any time by
order, remove the disqualification.
(4) Suspension- (a) If after the preliminary enquiry, the
Pradhan, Up pradhan, Pramukh, Up pramukh, Chairman, Vice
chairman found guilty in prima facie than till the final enquiry,
the State Government may suspend him.
(b) If it is proved that the meeting of Gram Sabha/ Gram
Panchayat is convened in the house of Pradhan/ Up Pradhan
than after enquiry against the concerning person, the State
Government may suspend him;
Provided that no order shall be passed adversely affecting
an person by the State Government/ designated authority unless
such person has been given an opportunity of making his
representation;
Provided further that the preliminary inquiry shall be
completed within one month and the final inquiry shall be
completed within six months, positively"
18. The very intention and purpose of the legislative intend
of Section 138 of the Act of 2016, is taken into consideration, for the
purpose of exercising the powers of removal of an elected Pradhan
from his Office has been vested with the "State Government".

10
19. In the definition clause of the Act, the State Government
has been independently defined under Sub-section (39) of Section 2 of
the Act, which reads as under :-
""State Government" means the Government of
Uttarakhand;"
20. On its simple analogy of the definition of State, it means
the Government of Uttarakhand. Meaning thereby, if the definition of
the State Government, is borrowed for the purposes of applying
Section 138 (1) (c), it will not include within its ambit the "District
Magistrate", who could have exercised the powers For the purposes
of removing the Pradhan under Section 138 (1) (c) and the logic
behind it, is that if the powers are vested by the special statute and
mandate of Constitution of India, as it has been, contemplated under
Article 243, of the Constitution of India, it is exclusively vested with
the "State Government", and obviously herein, would mean the
State Government defined under the Act. It will not include within
its definition the Collector or the District Magistrate, for the reason
being that the Legislature in its own wisdom has independently
defined the Collector and the District Magistrate under Sub-section
(20) of Section 2 of the Panchayat Raj Act of 2016, to be read with
Section 2, Sub-section (21), which means that the District Magistrate,
as he has been appointed under Section 20 of the Code of Criminal
Procedure. Meaning thereby, on a harmonious construction of
Sections 2 (20) and 2 (21) to be read with Section 2 (39) of the
Panchayat Raj Act of 2016, there is no doubt at all that the District
Magistrate defined under Sub-section (21) of Section 2 of the Act,
would not fall to be within the purview of the definition of the State,
which has been independently defined under Sub-section (39) of
Section 2 of the Panchayat Raj Act of 2016. Hence, on this limited
aspect itself, the powers exercised by the District Magistrate, for the
purposes of removal of the Pradhan from his elected office, apart from
the fact that it runs contrary to the provisions of Article 243-O of the

11
Constitution. The District Magistrate, as per the humble opinion of
this Court, will not fall to be a State, as it has been provided under
Section 138 of the Act of 2016, who could have removed the Pradhan
and hence, this Court hereby is of the opinion, that the District
Magistrate was not competent to pass the order invoking the provision
contained under Section 138 of the Panchayat Raj Act, which was
otherwise under the Act, was exclusively vested with the State, which
is altogether, a distinct entity under the Act.
21. Even otherwise, too the provisions of Section 138 (1) (c),
as it has been extracted above, it provides a certain mandatory
procedure which was required to be followed before removing an
elected Pradhan, under Section 138 (1) (c), i.e. the provision under
which the complaint has been filed. On its simplicitor reading, it
provides that on the receipt of the complaint, a "preliminary inquiry",
was required to be held on the basis of the which, the Pradhan could
be initially suspended, on the basis of the contents of the complaint, if
at all any prima facie case was made out, and that too, if he was found
to be guilty for the reason, which has been given therein under Section
138 (1) (c) itself. At this stage, itself, this Court feels it necessary to
observe that the ground of complaints, that the petitioner did not have
Class-VIII certificate or it was a fraudulent certificate, it might have
rendered her ineligible to contest the election, subject to its
establishment after the inquiry to be conducted as per law, after
placing petitioner under suspension not otherwise. But the same
would not fall to be within the set of allegations under, which the
provisions of Section 138 (1) (c) could have been attracted, because
no fact finding enquiry was conducted against the petitioner after
placing her under suspension, for the purposes of conducting an
inquiry. No such procedure was adhered to in the present case.
22. The action under the said Section could be taken only
where the elected Pradhan, has been found to be guilty during his
regime in the earlier terms of office as a Pradhan or was ultimately

12
established or found to have mis-conducted himself or herself, in the
discharge of her duties attached to the Office as a Pradhan or has
caused the loss and damages, to the funds of the Panchayat property,
or has caused loss or damages due to the conduct of work, as
unauthorised, in the place where he / she is posted as Pradhan.
23. On scrutinization of the said provisions, it nowhere
envisages to attract the provisions contained under Section 138 (1) (c),
on the ground that Class-VIII certificate of the petitioner was
fraudulently obtained by her, which was otherwise proved by the
documents on record, that it was issued by the competent authority,
i.e. the Principle of the Institution, and hence, that ground exclusively
will not fall to be within the grounds which are provided under
Section 138 (1) (c), which could have sustained the complaint filed by
the respondent No.3, particularly when :-
a) Regular Election Petition was pending, at the behest of
others.
b) Respondent No.3, has not challenged election by filing
any Election Petition.
24. There is another reason, as to why the complaint
submitted by respondent No. 3, under Section 138, would not be
maintainable, because prior to taking an action of removal
contemplated under Section 138 of the Act, as already referred above,
the power has been exclusively vested with the State and since the
State under the Act itself will not include within its definition the
District Magistrate, hence, the action would be vitiated and be without
any authority, under law. Apart from it, Section 138 of the Act, itself
contemplates, that on an establishment of the prima facie allegation
contained under 138 (1) (c) itself, the Pradhan would be initially
placed under suspension, subject to the completion of the final
inquiry, on the establishment of the misconduct of his / her work,
duties as Pradhan, she could be removed from the office, and that too
only after the culmination of the final inquiry, which has to be held

13
against the elected Pradhan, as per the procedure, provided under the
Act.
25. If the impugned order passed by District Magistrate in
the instant case is taken into consideration, in fact, there was a
complete non compliance of the provisions contained under Section
138 and the procedure contemplated therein. Apart from the fact, as
per the opinion of this Court, that the complaint, itself will not fall to
be within the purview of Section 138 (1) (c), because the District
Magistrate while passing the order has not recorded any finding at any
stage, that the preliminary inquiry or the final inquiry as provided
under Section 138 of the Act, was ever conducted against the
petitioner, for the purposes of ousting her from the elected office of
Pradhan under Section 138 (1) (c).
26. The respondents, in support of their contention, had made
reference to the U.P. Panchayat Raj Act, 1947, and the Rules framed
thereunder, which governs the procedure to be resorted to for the
purposes of the removal of the Pradhan from his / her office.
27. After having heard the counsel for the parties at length,
this Court is of the view, that with the enforcement of the Uttarakhand
Panchayati Raj Act, 2016, by virtue of its repealing Section contained
under Section 194, in fact, the provisions of the U.P. Panchayat Raj
Act, 1947, had been repealed. The effect of the repealment of the Act
of 1947, by virtue of the implications of Section 194 of the Act of
2016, would be that the Rules, which are subordinate legislation
framed under the rule making power provided under the then U.P.
Panchayat Raj Act of 1947, would not be saved to be applied, for the
removal of the Pradhan; until and unless, it is specifically saved to be
applied by the Uttarakhand Panchayati Raj Act of 2016, by
specifically stipulating it in the saving clause. Otherwise, this Court is
of the view that the subordinate legislation, loses its life and

14
enforceability, with the repealment of the principal Act under which it
has been framed, unless saved.
28. In order to answer the said query of the Court about the
savings Clause, where the Rules of 1947, whether it is still saved to be
applied in the State of Uttarakhand, after the enforcement of the
Uttarakhand Panchayati Act of 2016, the counsel for the respondents
had submitted that the Rules of removal of the Pradhan as provided
under the U.P. Panchayat Raj (Removal of Pradhan, Up-pradhan and
Members) Enquiry Rules, 1997, has been saved by virtue of the
subsequent amendment made in the Panchayat Raj Act, 2016, by
virtue of the amendment, which was notified in the Gazette
Notification on 20th January, 2020, whereby, by virtue of the
Uttarakhand Panchayati Raj Second Amendment Act, Sub-clause (35)
of Section 2 of the Act, which defines the Rules, initially, it meant the
Rules as framed by the State Government in the exercise of the
powers under this Act. The reference of this amending Act, prior to
the Amendment, of 20th January, 2020, would obviously mean the
Rules framed under the Panchayati Raj Act of 2016, but since, at the
time when the Act itself was enforced, the Rules of 1997, framed
under the U.P. Act were not saved, hence it would not have applied
till the actual amendment was notified to be carried by the State of
Uttarakhand by the Amending Act of 9 of 2020, w.e.f. 20.01.2020,
where Clause (35) of Section 2 of the Uttarakhand Panchayati Raj
(Second Amendment) Act, 2019, had provided as under:-
" 35 "Rules" means rules made under this Act but until
such rules are not promulgated under the Uttar Pradesh
Panchayati Raj Act, 1947 and the Uttar Pradesh Kshettra
Panchayat and Zila Panchayat Act, 1961;"
29. That Rules, herein, means that the Rules framed under
the Act of 2016, but the Rules as framed under the U.P. Panchayat Raj
Act of 1947, were not protected to be made applicable, till the State of

15
Uttarakhand itself promulgates the Rules itself, by amending Act
w.e.f. 20.01.2020. Hence, in the present case, since the complaint
being of 05.11.2019, the rules notified by gazette notification of
20.01.2020, would not apply to complaint filed prior to it, in violation
of Article 243-O of the Constitution of India.
30. Even otherwise there is nothing on record to show that
there happens to be any Rules framed by the State of Uttarakhand for
the purposes of removal of the elected Pradhan or Up-pradhan, and
consequently, the principles of the U.P. Panchayat Raj Rules 1997,
would apply. If that be the situation, in that eventuality, the procedure
for removal of Pradhan, even if it is presumed by attracting the
provisions contained under Section 138, apart from the fact, that it
could be exercised by the State and not by the District Magistrate,
hence, this Court holds, that the procedure for conducting the
preliminary inquiry and the final inquiry, therein, has been provided
under the Rules of 1997, which has been framed under Section 95 (1)
of the U.P. Panchayat Raj Act of 1947, would not apply under the
circumstances of the present case, where complaint of 05.11.2019, has
been instituted prior to amendment made w.e.f. 20.01.2020, as the
procedural law cannot be made applicable retrospectively.
31. If the impugned order passed by the District Magistrate is
taken into consideration, in fact, it does not satisfy the strict test of
procedure which has been even provided under the Rules of 1997,
which has been made applicable by the amendment of 20th January,
2020, as no preliminary inquiry provided under Rule 4 of Rule of
1997, was ever conducted after appointing the Inquiry Officer under
Rule 5 and conducting the inquiry under Rule 6 of the Rules, thus it
doesn't show that the procedure was ever adhered to and this in itself
would vitiate the entire proceedings itself.
32. There is another logic for not accepting the contention of
the learned counsel for the respondents, who are supporting the

16
impugned order, the reason being, that if Section 9 itself of the U.P.
Panchayat Raj Act, is taken into consideration, under the strength of
which, the Rules of 1997, have been framed, it had specifically
provided the power of suspension. Power of suspension was to be
resorted to as a first step during the pendency of the fact finding
inquiry in order to establish the set of allegations levelled against the
Pradhan so as to test the bona fides of the complaint. But, in the
instant case, there is not even a single piece of evidence on record, to
show that any of the allegations contained under Section 95 (1) (g),
particularly as contained in its proviso, under which, the Rules of
1997, has been framed, was ever complied with, because the
suspension of the Pradhan itself under the Rules of 1997, could be
only when satisfaction is recorded by the authority competent to
suspend, based on the prima facie of the establishment of the charge
levelled in the complaint.
33. Hence, in that view of the matter, if the Rules of 1997,
for a moment, it is taken into consideration, that if at all, it would be
applied in the light of the amendment by Act No. 20 of 2020, of State
of Uttarakhand, even then too, the grounds narrated therein, under
Section 95, i.e. under the Principal Act of the U.P. 1997, was not
existing, whereby the power of suspension could have been shown to
have been exercised, under the proviso to the said provisions.
34. Though the fact remains that in the instant case, in the
absence of there being any fact finding recorded even if under Section
95 of the old repealed Act of 1947, to the said effect, once the
Pradhan, has not been suspended on the set of allegations, though it
might be outside the ambit and scope of the allegation falling within
the domain of provisions contained under Section 138 (1) (c) and
Section 95, the impugned order passed by the District Magistrate,
would be vitiated.

17
35. Thus for the reasons aforesaid, the Writ Petition is
allowed and the relief claimed therein is granted.
